html:
Guyana (Netherlands) is the map's name for the Dutch colonies on the Guiana coast of South America in 1715, between the Orinoco and the Maroni rivers.

There were three of them, each on its own river: Essequibo, the oldest, under the Dutch West India Company; Berbice, run as a private colony by the Van Peere family of Vlissingen from 1627; and Surinam, taken from England in 1667. All grew sugar, coffee or cotton on plantations worked by enslaved Africans from the Atlantic slave trade, who far outnumbered the Europeans.

Resistance was constant. Runaways formed Maroon communities in the forest, and in the Berbice slave uprising of 1763 the enslaved held most of that colony for almost a year. In the wars after 1795 Britain took the western colonies and kept them in 1814; they became British Guiana. Surinam stayed Dutch as Dutch Guiana.
sum: Guyana (Netherlands) is the map's name for the Dutch colonies on the Guiana coast of South America in 1715, between the Orinoco and the Maroni rivers.
